name: Toast
description: A notification surface: title, description, one action and a close button; `<Toaster>` shows, times and stacks them.

title.description: Main line of the notification, in bold.

action.description: A button under the text; clicking it runs its onClick and then calls onClose.

tone.description: Border color: neutral, positive, warning or destructive; every tone is announced as a polite status. Default: neutral.

closable.description: Lets the user close the toast: a close button, and Escape inside the toast; both need `onClose`. Default: true.

buttonProps.description: Visual Button variant and style for both action and close controls.

props.title: Workspace updated
props.description: Your changes are available to collaborators.

props.title: Deployment completed
props.description: Production is healthy and serving the new release.

props.title: Usage is near the limit
props.description: This workspace has used 82% of its monthly quota.

props.title: Deployment failed
props.description: Review the build log before retrying.

behavior.timing: Each toast closes after its own duration (default 5000 ms; 0 keeps it). A pointer over a toast, focus in the region or a background window pauses every timer, keeping the time left.
behavior.stacking: Toaster shows the newest maxVisible toasts (default 3), newest nearest the viewport edge; older ones wait with their time stopped. toast({ id }) updates a shown toast in place.
behavior.closing: closable gives a close button and Escape inside the toast; both call onClose, so a Toast without onClose shows no close button. The action runs its onClick, then closes unless the click was prevented.

aria.toneRolePolicy: All toast tones stay non-blocking polite status messages. Use Modal or alertdialog for blocking alerts.
aria.region: Toaster is a polite live region named by a native aria-label, default 'Notifications (F8)'. Each toast is a status named by its title and described by its description.
aria.focus: A toast closed from the keyboard moves focus to its neighbour, and after the last one back to where focus came from.

notes: Toast content uses Text and Bar/Button primitives internally; do not create toast-local typography classes for new copy.
Toast surfaces use the shared overlay/dropdown background while semantic tones map the full border to monochrome feedback tokens.
Toaster is a fixed column clear of the safe-area insets; only the toasts take the pointer, and it renders the same public Toast surface on the shared --uf-z-toast layer.
